chapter_note: A short chapter with a clear two-layer structure. The substrate teaching (¶2-3) describes two cosmic powers—Mother of Life and First Man—grieving for their children/sons who are bound in Darkness and assaulted by enemies. This is pure cosmic-to-cosmic mapping: cosmic parent → cosmic offspring → cosmic bondage/conflict. The editorial layer (¶4-5) extends the enumeration pattern to Mani himself as 'the third one who grieves,' applying the cosmic grief template to his church community and unredeemed souls. The editorial seam at ¶4 is clean: the substrate enumeration ('The first...', 'The second...') is complete at two cosmic powers, and 'The third one who grieves am I' is Mani's self-insertion that extends the pattern to institutional content. Gardner notes the title promises four powers but only three appear, suggesting possible textual loss or compositional irregularity. The substrate portion is intact and coherent as a teaching about cosmic parental grief.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic opening ('Once again the enlightener speaks') followed by Mani's first-person self-identification as one of three cosmic grieving powers. While 'three powers that are heart-broken, who have come from the Father' gestures at cosmological content, it is entirely embedded within Mani's apostolic self-insertion ('I am one of they that grieve') and cannot be cleanly extracted without the first-person claim. This paragraph is the editorial hinge that allows extending a two-power substrate teaching to include Mani as a third cosmic griever.

paragraphs.core_text: The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poi]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [wa]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [s]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system: Mother of Life (cosmic parent) → her children (light elements) → conjoined with Darkness and poison (cosmic bondage) → bound with the ruling-power (cosmic hierarchy). Enumeration marker 'The first who grieves' is structural. High substrate score (13.51). The rhetorical question 'For what was she grieving...' is a teaching device within the substrate pedagogical tradition, not an editorial addition.

paragraphs.core_text: [The s]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [great]ness and kingdom is established in the li[ght] ship [...]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[ri]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate. First Man (cosmic being) in the light ship (cosmic geography) grieving for his five sons (five light elements) attacked by the enemy (forces of Darkness). Every mapping stays cosmic-to-cosmic. Enumeration marker 'The second one who is troubled' continues the teaching structure. The 'five sons' is a key substrate signature—the five-element system. The phrase 'the enemy who assaults them daily' describes ongoing cosmic conflict, not contemporary persecution. Low substrate vocabulary score (2.02) despite clearly substrate content—likely because the passage uses narrative/emotional language rather than technical terminology.

Editorial seam. 'The third one who grieves am I' mimics the substrate enumeration pattern ('The first...', 'The second...') but applies it to Mani and his institutional church. 'The holy church that I chose,' 'slavery of the authoritarians,' 'tribulation and persecution'—all reach outside the cosmic system into Mani's contemporary world. This is the classic pattern-extension seam: the substrate two-fold enumeration (Mother of Life, First Man) was complete, and the editor extended it to include Mani as a third griever for institutional purposes. The entire paragraph is one editorial act—not mixed.

Institutional extension. Mani's first-person pastoral concern for 'souls who have refused hope.' References to gehenna, repentance, and 'the right hand of peace and mercy that I brought from the Father' are all apostolic-missionary language. Institutional vocabulary score is highest in the chapter (9.33). This is the 'fourth grief' that the title may reference—but it is entirely within Mani's apostolic voice, not cosmic-to-cosmic mapping.
